claim: N-Methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDA-Rs) are ion channels that are important for synaptic plasticity.
source: N-Methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDA-Rs) are ion channels that are important for synaptic plasticity, which is involved in learning and drug addiction.
evidence: This is a statement about the biological function of NMDA-Rs, drawing from established scientific knowledge in neuroscience.

claim: Synaptic plasticity is involved in learning and drug addiction.
source: N-Methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDA-Rs) are ion channels that are important for synaptic plasticity, which is involved in learning and drug addiction.
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific consensus about the role of synaptic plasticity.

claim: Enzymatic targeting of MK801 to a molecularly defined neuronal population can be achieved with the cell-type-selectivity of genetic methods and the temporal control of pharmacology.
source: We show enzymatic targeting of an NMDA-R antagonist, MK801, to a molecularly defined neuronal population with the cell-type-selectivity of genetic methods and the temporal control of pharmacology.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NMDA-Rs on dopamine neurons are necessary for cocaine-induced synaptic potentiation.
source: We find that NMDA-Rs on dopamine neurons are necessary for cocaine-induced synaptic potentiation, demonstrating that cell type-specific pharmacology can be used to dissect signaling pathways within complex brain circuits.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from the cocaine-induced synaptic plasticity experiments.

claim: Cell type-specific pharmacology can be used to dissect signaling pathways within complex brain circuits.
source: We find that NMDA-Rs on dopamine neurons are necessary for cocaine-induced synaptic potentiation, demonstrating that cell type-specific pharmacology can be used to dissect signaling pathways within complex brain circuits.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results demonstrating the utility of the method.

claim: NMDA-Rs are glutamate-gated ion channels that are critical for the regulation of synaptic functions in the central nervous system.
source: N-Methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDA-Rs) are glutamate-gated ion channels that are critical for the regulation of synaptic functions in the central nervous system, such as synaptic plasticity (Malenka and Nicoll, 1993; Collingridge et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: NMDA-R dependent synaptic plasticity plays an important role in learning.
source: NMDA-R dependent synaptic plasticity plays an important role in learning.
evidence: This reflects established scientific knowledge about NMDA-R function.

claim: NMDA-R dependent synaptic plasticity is involved in sensitization of drug-related behaviors.
source: This includes learning that can also have maladaptive consequences, for example sensitization of drug-related behaviors (Kalivas and Alesdatter, 1993; Ungless et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: NMDA-Rs are expressed in most cell types in the brain.
source: However, because NMDA-Rs are expressed in most cell types in the brain (Conti et al., 1997; Verkhratsky and Kirchhoff, 2007), it is a considerable challenge to selectively assess the importance of NMDA-R mediated synaptic plasticity in specific cell types.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: It is a considerable challenge to selectively assess the importance of NMDA-R mediated synaptic plasticity in specific cell types.
source: However, because NMDA-Rs are expressed in most cell types in the brain (Conti et al., 1997; Verkhratsky and Kirchhoff, 2007), it is a considerable challenge to selectively assess the importance of NMDA-R mediated synaptic plasticity in specific cell types.
evidence: This is an inference based on the widespread expression of NMDA-Rs.

claim: Small molecule antagonists allow rapid blockade of NMDA-Rs.
source: Small molecule antagonists allow rapid blockade of NMDA-Rs, which has been critical for analyzing synaptic plasticity processes that operate over short timescales.
evidence: This reflects established knowledge about pharmacological tools.

claim: Existing pharmacological agents for NMDA-Rs are not cell type-selective.
source: However, existing pharmacological agents are not cell type-selective.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of current pharmacological tools, based on established knowledge.

claim: Genetic methods can be used for cell type-specific ablation of NMDA-R function by crossing to a mouse line with cell type-selective expression of Cre or by spatially targeted injection of Cre-expressing viral vectors.
source: Alternatively, genetic methods can be used, typically involving Cre-recombinase (Cre)-mediated excision of a loxP flanked exon in Grin1, which encodes a critical NMDA-R subunit that is required for channel function. This allows cell type-specific ablation of NMDA-R function by crossing to a mouse line with cell type-selective expression of Cre or by spatially targeted injection of Cre-expressing viral vectors.
evidence: This describes established genetic methods used in neuroscience research.

claim: Genetic methods for NMDA-R disruption are not fast and typically disrupt NMDA-Rs over timescales ranging from a week to the lifetime of an animal.
source: A major limitation is that genetic methods are not fast; they typically disrupt NMDA-Rs over timescales ranging from a week to the lifetime of an animal, during which time substantial compensatory effects in circuit function are observed (Engblom et al., 2008; Zweifel et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research demonstrating compensatory effects.

claim: Substantial compensatory effects in circuit function are observed during genetic disruption of NMDA-Rs.
source: A major limitation is that genetic methods are not fast; they typically disrupt NMDA-Rs over timescales ranging from a week to the lifetime of an animal, during which time substantial compensatory effects in circuit function are observed (Engblom et al., 2008; Zweifel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: MK801 is a potent non-competitive antagonist of NMDA-Rs.
source: MK801 is a potent non-competitive antagonist of NMDA-Rs that use-dependently blocks the channel in the open (glutamate-bound) state (Wong et al., 1986; Woodruff et al., 1987).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MK801 use-dependently blocks the NMDA-R channel in the open (glutamate-bound) state.
source: MK801 is a potent non-competitive antagonist of NMDA-Rs that use-dependently blocks the channel in the open (glutamate-bound) state (Wong et al., 1986; Woodruff et al., 1987).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: MK801 can bind and block the NMDA-R channel ion conductance pore from the intracellular compartment.
source: Furthermore, MK801 can bind and block the NMDA-R channel ion conductance pore from the intracellular compartment (Berretta and Jones, 1996; Bender et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A carboxymethylpropyl ester group has been used previously in brain tissue to mask a fluorophore and a kinesin inhibitor.
source: A carboxymethylpropyl ester group has been used previously in brain tissue to mask a fluorophore and a kinesin inhibitor, and extensive analysis showed that this group was stable to endogenous neuronal esterases but was cleaved in neurons transgenically expressing PLE (Tian et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The carboxymethylpropyl ester group is stable to endogenous neuronal esterases but is cleaved in neurons transgenically expressing PLE.
source: A carboxymethylpropyl ester group has been used previously in brain tissue to mask a fluorophore and a kinesin inhibitor, and extensive analysis showed that this group was stable to endogenous neuronal esterases but was cleaved in neurons transgenically expressing PLE (Tian et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: MK801 contains a secondary amine that is critical for NMDA-R antagonism.
source: Because MK801 contains a secondary amine that is critical for NMDA-R antagonism, we used a 4-hydroxy-3-nitrobenzyl carbamate (Gesson et al., 1994) to link MK801 and a carboxymethylpropyl ester to generate CM-MK801 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This reflects knowledge about the structure-activity relationship of MK801.

claim: Enzymatic cleavage of the CM ester inside neurons expressing PLE leads to spontaneous 1,6-elimination of the vinylogous hemiaminal, liberating MK801.
source: Enzymatic cleavage of the CM ester inside neurons expressing PLE leads to spontaneous 1,6-elimination of the vinylogous hemiaminal, liberating MK801 (Figure 1D).
evidence: This describes the chemical mechanism of MK801 liberation, which is a designed property of the molecule.

claim: CM-MK801 should be efficacious and completely block NMDA-Rs in PLE+ neurons.
source: Three critical properties of the CM-MK801/PLE system must be evaluated for cell type-specific pharmacology: 1) CM-MK801 should be efficacious and completely block NMDA-Rs in PLE+ neurons, 2) PLE− neurons should not unmask CM-MK801, and 3) unmasked MK801 should be confined to PLE+ neurons without affecting adjacent PLE− neurons.
evidence: This is a design criterion for the system that is subsequently tested experimentally.

claim: PLE− neurons should not unmask CM-MK801.
source: Three critical properties of the CM-MK801/PLE system must be evaluated for cell type-specific pharmacology: 1) CM-MK801 should be efficacious and completely block NMDA-Rs in PLE+ neurons, 2) PLE− neurons should not unmask CM-MK801, and 3) unmasked MK801 should be confined to PLE+ neurons without affecting adjacent PLE− neurons.
evidence: This is a design criterion for the system that is subsequently tested experimentally.

claim: Unmasked MK801 should be confined to PLE+ neurons without affecting adjacent PLE− neurons.
source: Three critical properties of the CM-MK801/PLE system must be evaluated for cell type-specific pharmacology: 1) CM-MK801 should be efficacious and completely block NMDA-Rs in PLE+ neurons, 2) PLE− neurons should not unmask CM-MK801, and 3) unmasked MK801 should be confined to PLE+ neurons without affecting adjacent PLE− neurons.
evidence: This is a design criterion for the system that is subsequently tested experimentally.

claim: PLE expression was well tolerated in cortical neurons.
source: Consistent with previous work, PLE expression was well tolerated in cortical neurons (Tian et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: CM-MK801 can completely block NMDA-R currents in neurons expressing the PLE transgene.
source: This shows that CM-MK801 can completely block NMDA-R currents in neurons expressing the PLE transgene.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing NMDA-R EPSC reduction in PLE+ neurons.

claim: In the presence of CM-MK801, PLE− neurons that were adjacent to PLE+ neurons showed scant reduction of QNMDA.
source: In contrast, in the presence of CM-MK801, PLE− neurons that were adjacent to PLE+ neurons showed scant reduction of QNMDA (Figure 2D,F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in the figures.

claim: The slight QNMDA reduction in PLE− neurons exposed to CM-MK801 was not significantly different than QNMDA in neurons in the absence of CM-MK801.
source: The slight QNMDA reduction in PLE− neurons exposed to CM-MK801 was not significantly different than QNMDA in neurons in the absence of CM-MK801 (QNMDA inhibition: PLE−/CM-MK801: 16% ± 8.9, n = 6; PLE+: 33% ± 8.6, n = 4; PLE−: 21% ± 6.3; ANOVA, F2,13 = 2.3, p = 0.15), thus QNMDA reduction in PLE− neurons was due to modest NMDA-R synaptic rundown (Rosenmund and Westbrook, 1993) and not an effect of MK801 in PLE− neurons.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: QNMDA reduction in PLE− neurons was due to modest NMDA-R synaptic rundown and not an effect of MK801 in PLE− neurons.
source: The slight QNMDA reduction in PLE− neurons exposed to CM-MK801 was not significantly different than QNMDA in neurons in the absence of CM-MK801 (QNMDA inhibition: PLE−/CM-MK801: 16% ± 8.9, n = 6; PLE+: 33% ± 8.6, n = 4; PLE−: 21% ± 6.3; ANOVA, F2,13 = 2.3, p = 0.15), thus QNMDA reduction in PLE− neurons was due to modest NMDA-R synaptic rundown (Rosenmund and Westbrook, 1993) and not an effect of MK801 in PLE− neurons.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data and supported by a citation about synaptic rundown.

claim: CM-MK801 can be targeted specifically to neurons expressing a transgenic esterase.
source: These results show that CM-MK801 can be targeted specifically to neurons expressing a transgenic esterase and that CM-MK801 is selective, where MK801, once liberated, is confined to the PLE-expressing cell population.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: MK801, once liberated, is confined to the PLE-expressing cell population.
source: These results show that CM-MK801 can be targeted specifically to neurons expressing a transgenic esterase and that CM-MK801 is selective, where MK801, once liberated, is confined to the PLE-expressing cell population.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing no effect in PLE− neurons.

claim: Cocaine and elevated dopamine leads to long-term synaptic potentiation of AMPA receptor-type synaptic currents in dopamine neurons in the ventral tegmental area.
source: Earlier work demonstrated that cocaine and elevated dopamine leads to long-term synaptic potentiation of AMPA receptor-type (AMPA-R) synaptic currents in dopamine (DA) neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA) (Ungless et al., 2001; Argilli et al., 2008) (Figure 3A), a key neuronal cell type associated with reward and addiction.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Dopamine neurons in the VTA are a key neuronal cell type associated with reward and addiction.
source: Earlier work demonstrated that cocaine and elevated dopamine leads to long-term synaptic potentiation of AMPA receptor-type (AMPA-R) synaptic currents in dopamine (DA) neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA) (Ungless et al., 2001; Argilli et al., 2008) (Figure 3A), a key neuronal cell type associated with reward and addiction.
evidence: This reflects established knowledge in neuroscience.

claim: Synaptic potentiation in DA neurons involved signaling through dopamine receptor 5, new protein synthesis, and insertion of AMPA-R subunits.
source: Further analysis demonstrated that synaptic potentiation involved signaling through dopamine receptor 5, new protein synthesis, and insertion of AMPA-R subunits (Argilli et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: NMDA-R blockade by systemic application of MK801 prevented synaptic potentiation in DA neurons.
source: These experiments also showed that NMDA-R blockade, by systemic application of MK801, prevented synaptic potentiation in DA neurons (Ungless et al., 2001) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Studies using dopamine neuron-specific knockout of Grin1 were confounded by compensatory effects in which synaptic AMPA-Rs were constitutively potentiated in DA neurons in the absence of cocaine.
source: To disrupt this process specifically in DA neurons, studies using dopamine neuron-specific knockout of Grin1 were performed but, in several instances, these were confounded by compensatory effects in which synaptic AMPA-Rs were constitutively potentiated in DA neurons in the absence of cocaine (Engblom et al., 2008; Zweifel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Virally mediated deletion of Grin1 showed compensatory effects within 1 week.
source: Even virally mediated deletion of Grin1 showed these compensatory effects within 1 week (Zweifel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Use of tamoxifen-activated Cre-ER for selective Grin1 ablation in DA neurons prevented a cocaine-induced shift in the rectification of AMPA-Rs after 1 week.
source: In contrast, another study found that use of tamoxifen-activiated Cre-ER for selective Grin1 ablation in DA neurons prevented a cocaine-induced shift in the rectification of AMPA-Rs after 1 week (Engblom et al., 2008), which indicated that dopamine neuron NMDA-Rs were required for cocaine-induced plasticity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Dopamine neuron NMDA-Rs were required for cocaine-induced plasticity.
source: In contrast, another study found that use of tamoxifen-activiated Cre-ER for selective Grin1 ablation in DA neurons prevented a cocaine-induced shift in the rectification of AMPA-Rs after 1 week (Engblom et al., 2008), which indicated that dopamine neuron NMDA-Rs were required for cocaine-induced plasticity.
evidence: This is an interpretation from a cited study.

claim: For brain slices treated with CM-MK801, AMPAR-mediated mEPSC amplitude was increased in PLE− VTA DA neurons following cocaine treatment.
source: For brain slices treated with CM-MK801, AMPAR-mediated mEPSC amplitude was increased in PLE− VTA DA neurons following cocaine treatment.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Synaptic potentiation was blocked in PLE+ neurons treated with cocaine, and the mEPSC amplitude was similar to that in PLE+ or PLE− neurons that were not exposed to cocaine.
source: Synaptic potentiation was blocked in PLE+ neurons treated with cocaine, and the mEPSC amplitude was similar to that in PLE+ or PLE− neurons that were not exposed to cocaine.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: mEPSC frequency was unaffected by cocaine or CM-MK801.
source: The frequency of mEPSCs in DA neurons was not affected by CM-MK801 or cocaine (Figure 3E, ANOVA F3,57 = 0.30, p = 0.82).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: The membrane properties of DA neurons after CM-MK801 exposure were indistinguishable in PLE+ or PLE− cells treated or untreated with cocaine.
source: In addition, the membrane properties of DA neurons after CM-MK801 exposure were indistinguishable in PLE+ or PLE− cells treated or untreated with cocaine, further indicating that CM-MK801 is not perturbative to resting neuronal properties.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CM-MK801 is not perturbative to resting neuronal properties.
source: In addition, the membrane properties of DA neurons after CM-MK801 exposure were indistinguishable in PLE+ or PLE− cells treated or untreated with cocaine, further indicating that CM-MK801 is not perturbative to resting neuronal properties.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing no changes in membrane properties.

claim: NMDA-Rs in DA neurons are necessary for cocaine-induced potentiation of synaptic AMPA-R currents in this cell type ex vivo.
source: Therefore, using cell type-specific pharmacology in an ex vivo preparation, these experiments demonstrate that NMDA-Rs in DA neurons are necessary for cocaine-induced potentiation of synaptic AMPA-R currents in this cell type ex vivo, which is consistent with a prior report that examined this problem using Cre-ER in vivo (Engblom et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and is consistent with prior research.

claim: Cell type-specific pharmacology approach can selectively block NMDA-Rs in a molecularly defined neuron population using an esterase–ester pair.
source: Taken together, these experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of a cell type-specific pharmacology approach to selectively block NMDA-Rs in a molecularly defined neuron population using an esterase–ester pair.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cell type-specific pharmacology for activating genetically engineered ion channels has been described.
source: Cell type-specific pharmacology for activating genetically engineered ion channels has been described (Slimko et al., 2002; Magnus et al., 2011), and here we demonstrate rapid cell type-specific blockade of a native ion channel with a small molecule.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: This study demonstrates rapid cell type-specific blockade of a native ion channel with a small molecule.
source: Cell type-specific pharmacology for activating genetically engineered ion channels has been described (Slimko et al., 2002; Magnus et al., 2011), and here we demonstrate rapid cell type-specific blockade of a native ion channel with a small molecule.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: MK801 was liberated only in PLE+ but not in neighboring PLE− neurons.
source: Our data indicates that MK801 was liberated only in PLE+ but not in neighboring PLE− neurons, showing that this approach can be used to block NMDARs with cellular specificity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The absence of a neighbor effect with CM-MK801/PLE is consistent with experiments targeting MK801 to individual neurons in a patch pipette.
source: The absence of a neighbor effect with CM-MK801/PLE is consistent with experiments targeting MK801 to individual neurons in a patch pipette (Bender et al., 2006).
evidence: This is an inference supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The aqueous solubility of CM-MK801 (5–10 μM) makes it less suitable for direct injection into the brain because of the requirement for elevated levels of co-solvents.
source: One limitation of the approach presented here is that the aqueous solubility of CM-MK801 (5–10 μM) make it less suitable for direct injection into the brain because of the requirement for elevated levels of co-solvents, such as dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) (>0.1%), which resulted in VTA-containing brain slices that were unsuitable for recordings.
evidence: This is a limitation identified from experimental observations.

claim: Elevated levels of DMSO (>0.1%) resulted in VTA-containing brain slices that were unsuitable for recordings.
source: One limitation of the approach presented here is that the aqueous solubility of CM-MK801 (5–10 μM) make it less suitable for direct injection into the brain because of the requirement for elevated levels of co-solvents, such as dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) (>0.1%), which resulted in VTA-containing brain slices that were unsuitable for recordings.
evidence: This is an observation from experimental work.

claim: Additional improvements to cell type-specific pharmacological techniques are needed to facilitate manipulations in mammalian brains in vivo.
source: Therefore, additional improvements to cell type-specific pharmacological techniques are needed to facilitate manipulations in mammalian brains in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the limitations identified in the study.

claim: Ex vivo approaches to rapidly disrupt NMDA-R signaling with cell type specificity have broad utility.
source: However, because functional NMDA receptors are widely expressed throughout the mammalian nervous system, ex vivo approaches to rapidly disrupt NMDA-R signaling with cell type specificity have broad utility.
evidence: This is an inference about the potential applications of the method.

claim: NMDA-Rs are expressed in both neurons and glia.
source: NMDA-Rs are expressed in both neurons and glia (Conti et al., 1997; Verkhratsky and Kirchhoff, 2007), and selective genetic access to these cell classes in the brain could allow for dissection of their relative role in synaptic function.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Selective genetic access to neurons and glia could allow for dissection of their relative role in synaptic function.
source: NMDA-Rs are expressed in both neurons and glia (Conti et al., 1997; Verkhratsky and Kirchhoff, 2007), and selective genetic access to these cell classes in the brain could allow for dissection of their relative role in synaptic function.
evidence: This is speculation about potential applications of the method.

claim: The strategy applied here for selective delivery of MK801 can be extended to other small molecules for use in brain tissue.
source: Finally, the strategy applied here for selective delivery of MK801 can be extended to other small molecules for use in brain tissue (Tian et al., 2012), allowing for an approach that combines chemistry, molecular genetics, and neurobiology to dissect cell signaling pathways in specific cell types in the central nervous system.
evidence: This is speculation about future applications, supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In utero electroporation of the bicistronic plasmid pCAG::PLE-IRES-mCherry into the developing mouse brain allowed PLE and mCherry co-expression in only a subset of cortical layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons.
source: In utero electroporation (IUE) of the bicistronic plasmid pCAG::PLE-IRES-mCherry into the developing mouse brain allowed PLE and mCherry co-expression in only a subset of cortical layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used and its outcome.

claim: The NMDA-R EPSC amplitude and mean NMDA-R charge transfer decreased in a use-dependent manner in PLE+ neurons to a level similar to treatment with AP5.
source: The NMDA-R EPSC amplitude (Figure 2C) and mean NMDA-R charge transfer (QNMDA: mean integrated current, Figure 2E) decreased in a use-dependent manner in PLE+ neurons to a level similar to treatment with the competitive NMDA-R antagonist D-(−)-2-amino-5-phosphonopentanoic acid (AP5, 100 µM) (Figure 2E–G; QNMDA inhibition: CM-MK801, 82% ± 4; AP5, 84% ± 4; n = 11; unpaired t test, p = 0.75).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis.

claim: DA neurons showed significantly elevated potentiation of mEPSC amplitudes in PLE−/GFP+ DA neurons in the presence of CM-MK801 after cocaine exposure.
source: As shown previously in VTA-containing brain slices exposed to cocaine (Argilli et al., 2008), DA neurons showed significantly elevated potentiation of mEPSC amplitudes in PLE−/GFP+ DA neurons in the presence of CM-MK801, which further demonstrates the lack of activity for CM-MK801 in PLE− neurons.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and is consistent with prior research.

claim: The elevated mEPSC amplitudes in PLE−/GFP+ DA neurons in the presence of CM-MK801 and cocaine further demonstrates the lack of activity for CM-MK801 in PLE− neurons.
source: As shown previously in VTA-containing brain slices exposed to cocaine (Argilli et al., 2008), DA neurons showed significantly elevated potentiation of mEPSC amplitudes in PLE−/GFP+ DA neurons in the presence of CM-MK801, which further demonstrates the lack of activity for CM-MK801 in PLE− neurons.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data.

claim: For PLE+/mCherry+ DA neurons in CM-MK801 and cocaine, mEPSC amplitudes were not elevated and were similar to PLE+ or PLE− DA neurons in CM-MK801 that had not been exposed to cocaine.
source: Strikingly though, for PLE+/mCherry+ DA neurons in CM-MK801 and cocaine, mEPSC amplitudes were not elevated and were similar to PLE+ or PLE− DA neurons in CM-MK801 that had not been exposed to cocaine. (Figure 3D; Coc+/PLE−, 19.9 ± 0.9 pA, n = 17; Coc+/PLE+, 12.7 ± 0.8 pA, n = 14; Coc−/PLE−, 13.9 ± 0.6 pA, n = 12; Coc−/PLE+, 12.8 ± 0.7 pA, n = 15; ANOVA F3,57 = 19.0, p < 0.001).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis.
